page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7a.2xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by the KVM hypervisor and AMD EPYC 7T83 processors running at a base clock speed of 2.55 GHz. It offers 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, providing 32 MB of shared L3 cache and support for standard x86_64 instruction sets including AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance is provisioned with 16.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include bundled local disk storage or dedicated GPU acceleration, relying on remote block storage for persistent data operations.

Performance benchmarks show strong results in single-core compute tests, with stress-ng single-core performance ranking in the top 25% across comparable systems. General system benchmarks demonstrate balanced mid-range capacity, achieving a Geekbench multi-core score of 5,771 and a PassMark CPU score of 11,819.39. While small-block cached read bandwidth reaches 516.94 GB/sec, uncached large-block write operations are relatively constrained at 18.88 GB/sec. Similarly, while lightweight AI inference processes 686.22 prompt tokens per second on 135M models, heavier 7B model prompt processing drops to 17.15 tokens per second due to the lack of hardware accelerators and restricted memory write throughput.

With a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth and no local storage overhead, the ecs.c7a.2xlarge offers a cost-efficient resource profile for compute-centric workloads that do not demand high memory capacity per core. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures stable execution environments without noisy-neighbor contention. This server configuration fits Clang compilation pipelines, static web serving clusters, intermediate microservices, caching layers like Redis, and batch compression tasks.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7a.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance driven by an AMD EPYC 7T83 processor clocked at 2.55 GHz on x86_64 architecture. Configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores and 16.0 GB of RAM, it maintains a compute-focused 1:2 CPU-to-memory ratio. The instance excludes bundled local storage and GPU hardware, utilizing external storage alongside a 2 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results indicate strong single-core compute capabilities in stress-ng evaluations, complemented by solid multi-core processing in Clang compilation and ray tracing workloads. Large-block write memory throughput and larger LLM inference speeds are constrained, reflecting the lack of acceleration hardware and moderate memory bandwidth. Delivering stable dedicated vCPU allocation without memory excess, ecs.c7a.2xlarge is suited for application compilation, batch data compression, static web delivery, and intermediate backend microservices.
